author: Ahmed Ibrahim
title: Medvedev Fined at US Open for On-Court Conduct & Racket Abuse
text:
Daniil Medvedev Fined Heavily After U.S. Open Outburst The U.S. Open levied a considerable $42,500 fine against Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday, representing over a third of his $110,000 tournament prize money, following a heated display of frustration during a first-round loss.
The incident, presided over by tournament referee Jake Garner, resulted in a $30,000 penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct and an additional $12,500 for racket destruction . After the match concluded, Medvedev repeatedly slammed his racket against his chair along the sideline, ultimately shattering it.
The former world No. 1,and 2021 Flushing Meadows champion,reportedly became incensed on Sunday evening when chair umpire Greg Allensworth permitted his opponent,Benjamin Bonzi,a second chance at a first serve.This decision stemmed from a photographer moving within the court area despite being instructed not to do so.
Bonzi was on the verge of victory,leading 5-4 in the third set,when the photographer – whose credentials were afterward revoked – began walking along the side of the court at Louis Armstrong Stadium immediately after a fault. Allensworth directed the photographer to leave the court and then announced Bonzi would be awarded another first serve due to the disruption.
Did you know? – Medvedev’s fine is one of the largest ever issued at the U.S. Open for on-court conduct. Previous fines for similar offenses have typically fallen in the $10,000 to $20,000 range. Medvedev approached the umpire to voice his complaint, and the situation quickly escalated. The crowd responded with boos and chants of “Second serve!” The match was halted for over six minutes as Medvedev engaged with fans and directed insults toward Allensworth.
“He wants to go home, guys. He doesn’t like being here. He gets paid by match, not by hour,” Medvedev reportedly shouted over the microphones near the chair.
Despite the disruption, Medvedev managed to win the third and fourth sets.However, Bonzi ultimately prevailed with a final score of 6-3, 7-5, 6-7 (5), 0-6, 6-4.
pro tip: – Players can appeal fines issued by tournament officials. The appeal process involves submitting a written statement and potentially attending a hearing with a review panel. This loss marks Medvedev’s third consecutive first-round defeat at a Grand Slam tournament, including a similar outcome against Bonzi last month at Wimbledon .
The incident raises questions about the pressures faced by top-tier athletes and the boundaries of acceptable conduct on the court. It also highlights the increasing scrutiny on officials’ decisions and the impact of external factors – in this case, a photographer’s actions – on match outcomes.
Reader question: – Do you think umpires face undue pressure in high-profile matches? What measures could be taken to support them? Share your thoughts. Here’s a breakdown answering the “Why, Who, What, and How” questions:
Who: Daniil Medvedev, Benjamin Bonzi, chair umpire Greg Allensworth, and a photographer.
What: Daniil medvedev was fined $42,500 for unsportsmanlike conduct and racket destruction following a first-round loss at the U.S. Open. The incident stemmed from a dispute over a replayed first serve awarded to Bonzi due to a photographer’s disruption.
Why: Medvedev became enraged when Allensworth allowed Bonzi a second serve after a photographer walked across the court during a point. he felt the decision was unfair and voiced his frustration aggressively towards the umpire and the crowd.
